title: The Battle of Hunayn
subtitle: The Dawn Ambush, the Prophetic Stand upon the White Mule, and the Descent of Sakinah
summary: Descending into the narrow rocky gorge of Wadi Hunayn at dawn, the Muslim vanguard walked into a devastating concealed ambush laid by Hawazin archers. As arrow volleys triggered widespread panic and retreat across the frontline, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood immovable in the center of the storm upon his white mule Duldul, boldly proclaiming his prophetic mission. Summonsed by the thunderous voice of Al-Abbas, the believers rallied with ferocious courage, turning imminent catastrophe into total triumph.

sections.text: The Deadly Ambush in the Canyons

In the pre-dawn darkness of Wednesday, the tenth of Shawwal, the Muslim vanguard, commanded by Khalid ibn al-Walid and comprising the cavalry of Banu Sulaym, began its descent into the narrow, winding ravine of Wadi Hunayn. Unbeknownst to the advancing columns, Malik ibn Awf had occupied the steep basalt ridges, concealed ravines, and narrow defiles during the night. Thousands of Hawazin archers and swordsmen lay silently in ambush, arrows nocked to their bows, awaiting the precise moment of maximum vulnerability.

As the Muslim cavalry entered the deepest bottleneck of the gorge, a sudden, deafening war cry erupted from the cliffs above. A devastating, black hail of arrows rained down simultaneously from every direction, striking horses and riders without warning. Immediately following the barrage, disciplined columns of Hawazin infantry charged down the slopes with drawn swords, striking directly into the disorganized columns.
The Shock of Retreat and the Chaos of Battle

Panic rippled instantaneously through the vanguard. Terrified warhorses reared and bucked, colliding in the narrow passage, while the newly converted Makkan contingents and bedouin auxiliaries broke rank and fled backward in disarray. The retreating cavalry crashed into the advancing infantry columns, creating widespread confusion across the entire army. Some of the recent converts from Quraysh, still clinging to remnants of tribal resentment, remarked upon the retreat; Abu Sufyan remarked: 'Their flight will not stop until they reach the sea!'

While thousands retreated around him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood entirely unshaken in the absolute center of the vortex. Seated upon his white mule Duldul, accompanied by only a handful of steadfast companions—including Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Al-Abbas, and Usama ibn Zayd—the Prophet did not yield a single inch. In an act of unparalleled valor that defies all worldly military logic, the Prophet spurred his mount forward toward the oncoming ranks of Hawazin.

As Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith held the bridle of the mule and Al-Abbas held the stirrup trying to restrain him from charging directly into the enemy lines, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his blessed voice, proclaiming to all of Arabia his absolute certainty and divine authenticity:

أَنَا النَّبِيُّ لاَ كَذِبْ، أَنَا ابْنُ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبْ
'I am the Prophet, there is no lie! I am the son of Abdul-Muttalib!' (Sahih al-Bukhari 4315; Sahih Muslim 1776)

Al-Bara' ibn Azib later testified in Sahih al-Bukhari: 'By Allah, when the fighting became intensely ferocious, we sought protection behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the bravest among us was he who stood parallel to him in battle.'

Recognizing that the battle hung by a thread, the Prophet turned to his uncle Al-Abbas, who possessed an exceptionally thunderous, resonant voice, and commanded: 'O Abbas, call out to the companions of the Samurah tree! Call out to the companions of Surah Al-Baqarah!'

Al-Abbas bellowed with all the strength of his lungs across the canyon: 'O companions of the Tree! O companions of Surah Al-Baqarah! Where are you? The Messenger of Allah is here!' In an authentic narration in Sahih Muslim, Al-Abbas recalled: 'By Allah, when they heard my voice, they turned back like cows turning toward their calves, shouting: 'Labbayk! Labbayk!' (Here we are! At your service!).' Warriors whose horses refused to turn in the narrow pass leaped off their saddles, severed their horses' tethers, and ran on foot with swords drawn straight toward the sound of the Prophet's voice.
The Descent of Divine Sakinah and the Rout of Hawazin

Within minutes, a hundred veteran Ansar and Muhajirun formed an unbreakable iron wall around the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, engaging the charging forces of Hawazin in brutal hand-to-hand combat. Looking upon the ferocious clash of swords, the Prophet remarked: 'Now the battle has grown intensely heated' (Al-ana hamiya al-watees). Taking a handful of desert pebbles, the Prophet cast them toward the enemy ranks, saying: 'May these faces be disfigured!' (Shahat al-wujuh).

At that divine moment, the tide turned completely. Allah sent down His celestial tranquility (Sakinah) upon the hearts of the believers, accompanied by unseen angelic hosts that broke the psychological resolve of Hawazin, exactly as described in Surah At-Tawbah:

ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَعَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَأَنْزَلَ جُنُودًا لَمْ تَرَوْهَا وَعَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ الْكَافِرِينَ
'Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down soldiers you did not see and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the reward of the disbelievers.' (Surah At-Tawbah 9:26)

The ranks of Hawazin shattered completely. Realizing the day was lost, their warriors broke and fled in wild panic across the mountains, abandoning their families, herds, and all their earthly possessions upon the battlefield, exactly as the elder Duraid had forewarned. The Battle of Hunayn ended in a crushing victory for the believers, demonstrating that true triumph is forged not through sheer numbers, but through unshakeable faith and divine tranquility.
